source_text: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἰ καὶ ταυτολογεῖ ὁ Κέλσος περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ. δεύτερον ἤδη λέγων πλημμελήσαντα αὐτὸν δεδωκέναι παρὰ Ἰουδαίοις δίκην, ἀλλ᾿ ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἐπαναληψόμεθα τὴν ἀπολογίαν, ἀρκούμενοι τῇ προειρημένῃ. εἶτ᾿ ἐπεὶ ὡς ἕωλα τὰ περὶ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν καὶ κρίσεως θεοῦ καὶ τιμῆς μὲν ἐπὶ τοὺς δικαίους πυρὸς δ᾿ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀδίκους εὐτελίζει ὁ παρ᾿ αὐτῷ Ἰουδαῖος, μηδὲν δὲ καινὸν ἐν τούτοις διδάσκεσθαι φάσκων χριστιανοὺς οἴεται ἀνατρέπειν χριστιανισμόν· λεκτέον πρὸς αὐτὸν ὅτι ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἡμῶν, ὁρῶν Ἰουδαίους μηδὲν ἄξιον τῶν ἐν τοῖς προφήταις μαθημάτων πράττοντας, ἐδίδαξε διὰ παραβολῆς ὅτι „ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ“ „ἀρθήσεται“ μὲν ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνων „καὶ δοθήσεται“ τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν. διὸ καὶ ἔστιν ἀληθῶς ἰδεῖν πάντα μὲν τὰ Ἰουδαίων τῶν νῦν μύθους καὶ λήρους (οὐ γὰρ ἔχουσι τὸ φῶς τῆς γνώσεως τῶν γραφῶν), τὰ δὲ Χριστιανῶν ἀλήθειαν, ἐπᾶραι καὶ μετεωρίσαι ἀνθρώπου που ψυχὴν καὶ νοῦν δυνάμενα καὶ πείθοντα ἔχειν τι „πολίτευμα“ οὐχ ὅμοιον τοῖς κάτω Ἰουδαίοις κάτω που ἀλλ᾿ „ἐν οὐρανοῖς“· ὅπερ φαίνεται παρὰ τοῖς τὸ μέγεθος τῶν ἐν τῷ νόμῳ καὶ τοῖς προφήταις νοημάτων θεωροῦσι καὶ ἄλλοις παραστῆσαι δυναμένοις.
pass_a_gloss: After these things, even if Celsus repeats himself (ταυτολογεῖ) about Jesus, saying already a second time that he, having done wrong (πλημμελήσαντα), paid the penalty (δεδωκέναι δίκην) among/at the hands of the Jews, yet we shall not take up again (ἐπαναληψόμεθα) the defence (ἀπολογία), being content (ἀρκούμενοι) with the one said before. Then, since the Jew in his work disparages (εὐτελίζει) as stale/day-old (ἕωλα) the things about the resurrection of the dead (ἀνάστασις νεκρῶν) and judgment of God (κρίσις θεοῦ) and honour (τιμή) on the righteous but fire (πῦρ) on the unrighteous, and, asserting that Christians are taught nothing new (καινόν) in these, thinks he overturns (ἀνατρέπειν) Christianity (χριστιανισμός): it must be said to him that our Jesus, seeing the Jews doing nothing worthy of the teachings (μαθήματα) in the prophets, taught through a parable (παραβολή) that 'the kingdom of God' 'will be taken' (ἀρθήσεται) from them 'and will be given' (δοθήσεται) to those from the nations (ἔθνη). Therefore one can truly see all the things of the present Jews to be myths and nonsense (μῦθοι, λῆροι) (for they do not have the light of the knowledge (φῶς τῆς γνώσεως) of the Scriptures), but the things of Christians truth (ἀλήθεια), able to lift up and raise aloft (ἐπᾶραι, μετεωρίσαι) the soul and mind (ψυχή, νοῦς) of a man, and persuading [him] to have a 'citizenship/commonwealth' (πολίτευμα) not like the Jews below, somewhere below (κάτω που), but 'in the heavens'; which appears among those who contemplate (θεωροῦσι) the greatness of the meanings/thoughts (νοήματα) in the law and the prophets and are able to present (παραστῆσαι) [them] to others.
pass_b_english: After this, although Celsus repeats himself about Jesus, saying now for the second time that he did wrong and paid the penalty at the hands of the Jews, we will not repeat our defence, but rest content with what we said before.

Next, his Jew belittles as stale the teaching about the resurrection of the dead, the judgment of God, and honour for the righteous but fire for the unrighteous; and by claiming that Christians are taught nothing new in these matters, he thinks he overturns Christianity. We must say to him that our Jesus, seeing that the Jews were doing nothing worthy of the lessons in the prophets, taught by a parable that “the kingdom of God” would be “taken away” from them “and given” to those from the Gentiles (Matthew 21:43). That is why one can truly see that all the teachings of the Jews of today are myths and idle talk, for they do not have the light of the knowledge of the Scriptures, while the teachings of Christians are truth. These are able to lift up and raise on high the soul and mind of a human being, and they persuade him to have a “citizenship” not like that of the Jews, somewhere here below, but “in heaven” (Philippians 3:20). This is evident among those who contemplate the greatness of the meanings in the law and the prophets, and who are able to present them to others.

choices.why: No change: all clauses, negations and attributions match the Greek; Matthew 21:43 and Philippians 3:20 checked against the verse wording.

anf_compare.notes: Crombie (ANF 1872) and Chadwick (1953) were not used or consulted; English is from the Greek.

notes: Translated from the Greek of the staged Koetschau row only; Crombie (ANF) and Chadwick were not used.
Independent clause review: every clause checked; verdict pass.
Scripture citations sit inline beside the clause in Pass B.

translator_notes: The full stop printed after Ἰησοῦ in the staged text is treated as a comma; the sentence continues. Celsus’s charge in the first sentence is indirect speech in the Greek, so it is not put in quotation marks. Matthew 21:43 (end of the parable of the tenants, Matthew 21:33-43) reads ἀρθήσεται ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει; Origen paraphrases with ‘those from the Gentiles’. ‘The light of the knowledge’ may echo 2 Corinthians 4:6 (φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως); not certain enough for an inline citation. The text repeats κάτω (‘below ... somewhere below’), possibly a scribal doubling; rendered once as ‘somewhere here below’. Origen’s polemic against the Jews of his day is translated as written, without softening.
